title: Air Combat 3D — AI Productivity Case Study
subtitle: 3D Multiplayer Combat Game with Three.js, WebSockets, Docker & Generative AI Acceleration
summary: Empirical study measuring generative AI productivity gains in full-stack engineering. 3D multiplayer flight combat game built with Three.js, Node.js WebSockets, Docker, and Render.com (-40% dev time).
overview: Conducted as an empirical study to measure the impact of generative AI tools on full-stack developer productivity. Built a full 3D multiplayer aerial combat browser game from scratch using Three.js and WebSockets, establishing a quantitative benchmark for modern AI-assisted software delivery.
roleDescription: Solutions Architect, Full-Stack Developer & DevOps Engineer.
responsibilities: Full-Stack Architecture: Built interactive Three.js 3D flight canvas and Node.js backend handling matchmaking and real-time state synchronization via WebSockets.
DevOps Engineering: Containerized the entire application stack with Docker and automated continuous cloud deployment on Render.com.
Workflow Research: Formulated benchmarking methodology integrating AI-native IDEs (Cursor, Trae) to measure cycle time reductions against baseline development.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Maintaining multi-client real-time positional synchronization with low latency across web clients.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Built an optimized server-side authoritative game loop in Node.js broadcasting delta states over persistent WebSocket connections.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Empirically validating developer velocity improvements from generative AI assistants.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Tracked milestone delivery hours across 3D math, networking, containerization, and cloud deployment, demonstrating a ~40% reduction in end-to-end delivery time.

futureEvolution: Persistent player leaderboards and score history using PostgreSQL or Redis.
Private game rooms and additional multiplayer modes (such as Team Deathmatch).
